intro: Lesson 34: Bridge: 1.1 key events of the Prophet's ﷺ early life and marriage (Qur'an 66:1-3). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

timeline.label: c. 570 CE
timeline.text: Born in Makkah; father Abdullah already died

timeline.label: Infancy
timeline.text: Nursed by Halimah in the desert

timeline.label: Age 8
timeline.text: Grandfather Abd al-Muttalib dies; Abu Talib cares for him

timeline.label: c. 12
timeline.text: Trade trip to Syria; monk Bahira

panels.title: Youth, work and character
points: Joined Hilf al-Fudul to protect the wronged
Settled the Black Stone dispute at 35

panels.title: Set passage: Qur'an 66:1-3
points: 66:1: why forbid yourself what Allah made lawful?
66:2: Allah has given a way to release oaths
66:3: a private matter told to one wife was shared

blocks.h: Place eight events from birth to marriage

blocks.answers: In order: born c. 570 CE; nursed by Halimah; Aminah dies at 6; Abd al-Muttalib dies at 8, Abu Talib cares for him; trade trip to Syria c. 12; Hilf al-Fudul; trades Khadijah's goods honestly; marries Khadijah at 25. (The Black Stone dispute at 35 comes after the marriage.)

keywords.def: the Prophet's ﷺ clan within Quraysh
the trustworthy, his title before prophethood
a Christian monk who recognised signs of prophethood
a respected businesswoman who became his first wife

questions.q: Explain how ONE event from his early life prepared him to be trusted with the message.
questions.a: For example: the Black Stone: his fair solution showed wisdom and trust, so people knew he was honest and fair before he brought the message.

questions.q: At what age did he marry Khadijah, as commonly reported?
Which set passage is linked to 1.1?
Timeline and explain (pupil PDF): place eight events from birth to marriage, then in the portal response box explain two ways his early life prepared him for prophethood.
questions.a: Accurate timeline; two developed explanations (orphanhood and trust in Allah, 93:6-8; honesty in trade; Hilf al-Fudul and justice; Black Stone and wisdom).

questions.q: Extend: what does 66:1-3 show about the Prophet's ﷺ family life?
questions.a: He was human with a real family; Allah guided him; trust in marriage matters.

questions.q: Stretch: why might Allah have chosen someone with a known honest record?
questions.a: So people could not accuse him of lying; his character was a proof of his truthfulness.

questions.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ solve the dispute over the Black Stone?
options: He placed it on a cloak so every clan lifted it
He placed it alone without asking
He delayed it for a year
questions.a: A) He placed it on a cloak so every clan lifted it. Every clan shared the honour, which prevented fighting. This showed wisdom and fairness, part of why he was trusted.

questions.q: Who cared for him after his grandfather died?
Think again: what made him trustworthy?
questions.a: His record: honesty in trade, fairness, keeping trusts, known as al-Amin.
